rules.source: New York SHIELD Act (signed July 25, 2019), amending the 2005 breach statute — https://ag.ny.gov/resources/organizations/data-breach-reporting/shield-act
rules.retrieved_snippet: NY AG: covered entities holding New York residents' private information must notify affected consumers as quickly as possible after a breach (breach definition covers unauthorized access); report goes to AG, Department of State and State Police via AG portal; penalties up to $20 per failed notice capped at $250,000, and up to $5,000 per violation for inadequate safeguards.

rules.source: New York City Local Law 144 of 2021 (automated employment decision tools), enforced by DCWP — https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dca/downloads/pdf/about/DCWP-AEDT-FAQ.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: NYC DCWP: effective Jan. 1, 2023, enforcement from July 5, 2023; employers/agencies may not use an AEDT for hiring or promotion in NYC unless it had a bias audit within one year, a summary is posted publicly, and candidates are notified at least ten business days before use.
